officialTitle: Trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy for operable HER2-positive breast cancer (joint analysis of NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: In all, 4,046 patients with HER2-positive operable breast cancer were enrolled to receive doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel with or without trastuzumab in both trials.
design.notes: Joint analysis compared AC→paclitaxel (B-31 group 1 and N9831 group A) with the same regimen plus 52 weeks of trastuzumab started with paclitaxel (B-31 group 2, N9831 group C). N9831 sequential arm (group B) excluded.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding 1 year of trastuzumab, started concurrently with paclitaxel after AC, improve outcomes in operable HER2-positive breast cancer?

pico.population: Women with surgically removed HER2-positive breast cancer
pico.intervention: Doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel plus 52 weeks of trastuzumab beginning with paclitaxel
pico.outcomes: Primary: DFS. Secondary: OS, cardiac events

arms.label: AC → paclitaxel + trastuzumab
arms.regimen: Doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, then paclitaxel with concurrent trastuzumab for 52 weeks

publications.title: Trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy for operable HER2-positive breast cancer.
publications.label: First joint interim analysis

publications.title: Trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-positive breast cancer: planned joint analysis of overall survival from NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831.
publications.label: Planned definitive joint OS analysis

outcomes.experimentalValue: 133 events; absolute DFS difference 12 percent at three years
outcomes.sourceQuote: Of these, 133 were in the trastuzumab group and 261 in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.48; P<0.0001). This result crossed the early stopping boundary. The absolute difference in disease-free survival between the trastuzumab group and the control group was 12 percent at three years.

outcomes.experimentalValue: 33 percent reduction in the risk of death
outcomes.sourceQuote: Trastuzumab therapy was associated with a 33 percent reduction in the risk of death (P=0.015).

outcomes.analysisLabel: Definitive OS analysis (median time on study 8.4 years)
outcomes.sourceQuote: Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy led to a 37% relative improvement in OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.73; P < .001) and an increase in 10-year OS rate from 75.2% to 84%.

outcomes.analysisLabel: Definitive OS analysis (median time on study 8.4 years)
outcomes.sourceQuote: These results were accompanied by an improvement in DFS of 40% (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.68; P < .001) and increase in 10-year DFS rate from 62.2% to 73.7%.

safety.description: 3-year cumulative incidence of class III/IV congestive heart failure or cardiac death (trastuzumab group; B-31, with N9831 2.9 percent)
safety.sourceQuote: The three-year cumulative incidence of class III or IV congestive heart failure or death from cardiac causes in the trastuzumab group was 4.1 percent in trial B-31 and 2.9 percent in trial N9831.

strengths: Two large randomised trials combined in a prespecified joint analysis
limitations: Joint analysis was introduced by protocol amendment

clinicalImplications.text: Established adjuvant trastuzumab with chemotherapy as standard care for operable HER2-positive breast cancer, with durable disease-free and overall survival benefits.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Concurrent start of trastuzumab with the taxane (after AC) was the tested schedule; baseline and on-treatment cardiac monitoring matters given the reported heart-failure incidence.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 16236738 and 25332249. The 2014 abstract prints P values as '< .001', retained verbatim in pValue.
